text.title: Conversion Tracking Worked Example
text.summary: One complete tracking config for an e-commerce site sending to GA4, Google Ads and Meta: events.yml enforced in CI, Consent Mode v2 with EU and GB denied defaults, a server container on gtm.example.com forwarding the browser identifiers, three events (purchase with transaction_id dedup, sign_up with a hashed email for matching, funnel_step browser-only) and fixtures run in three browsers plus an ad-blocker profile, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the config as it is usually shipped and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: example.com sells online and runs paid search and Meta campaigns. Checkout tracking v3 (PR-2214) adds server-side sends through a GTM server container so purchases survive ad blockers. EU and UK visitors need consent before any tag; the order id `ORD-104233` is the identifier finance reconciles against.

example.title: checkout tracking v3
example.note: Every event is an `events.yml` entry with its conversion role per destination, and CI fails on a name that is not there (r-event-registry-single-source). `purchase` and `sign_up` are the recommended names, not `order_completed` or `signup`, so the built-in ecommerce and lead reports work; all names and parameters are inside the 40-character and 25-parameter limits (r-ga4-naming-and-parameter-limits). `purchase` carries `value`, `currency` and `transaction_id`, and `transaction_id` is the dedup field, so a reloaded thank-you page and the server copy collapse to one order in GA4, Meta and Google Ads (r-monetary-conversion-carries-transaction-id). Both dual-sent events have a `dedup` block, and the server container forwards `_fbp`, `_fbc`, the `_ga` client_id and the session_id rather than minting ids (r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers). Consent defaults with all four signals go before the config call; EU and GB default to denied, the rest of the world to granted, and the server honours the same state (r-consent-state-before-any-tag). No parameter is PII; the `em` sent to Meta for matching is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised email, and the example payloads contain no address or phone (r-no-pii-in-parameters). The endpoint is `gtm.example.com`, a subdomain of the site, with HttpOnly cookies, which is what keeps Safari's cookie beyond 7 days (r-server-endpoint-first-party-domain). Each event has a fixture with results for Chrome, Safari, Firefox and the ad-blocker profile on every destination it targets; `funnel_step` is browser-only, so the ad-blocker row honestly shows `seen: false` and the record says so (r-qa-fixtures-per-tracking-change).

example.title: the same change as usually shipped
example.note: What the validator prints: `registry.enforced_in_ci` is false (r-event-registry-single-source); consent defaults are pushed after config, `ad_user_data` and `ad_personalization` are missing, and the server ignores consent (r-consent-state-before-any-tag); the endpoint is not a subdomain of example.com, cookies are not HttpOnly, `_fbp`, `_fbc` and `session_id` are not forwarded, and the server mints a UUID per hit (r-server-endpoint-first-party-domain, r-browser-server-dedup-and-identifiers); `Order_Completed` is not snake_case and the second name is 53 characters (r-ga4-naming-and-parameter-limits); the `email` parameter is `pii: true` (r-no-pii-in-parameters); the monetary event has no `dedup` block (r-monetary-conversion-carries-transaction-id); QA ran in Chrome only without the ad-blocker profile (r-qa-fixtures-per-tracking-change). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: the monetary event lacks `transaction_id` and `currency`, `order_completed` is a synonym of the recommended `purchase`, the example payload carries an email address and a phone number, and the second event has no fixture at all. What the reviewer sees: purchases counted twice in Ads Manager, new users doubled in GA4, and EEA conversions Google Ads will refuse to measure (double-counted-conversions, fresh-client-id-server-side, tags-fire-before-consent).
